newsitem.title: UK: First Choice says no Canada unit offer plan.
newsitem.headline: First Choice says no Canada unit offer plan.

text.p: UK tour operator First Choice Holidays Plc said on Wednesday that it had no plans to sell its Canadian subsidiary after the unit's lower-than-expected profits in the year ended October 31.
Revenue from Signature Vacations is central to the company's strategy since it provides revenue outside the main holiday season for UK customers, a company spokesman said.

Operating profits of Signature Vacations fell to 2.4 million stg in 1995/96 from last year's record profits of 7.9 million. The group posted a full-year pre-tax profit of 10 million stg against 1.3 million in 1995.
The company, the UK's third largest tour operator by market share after Thomson and Airtours, also said it had no plans to buy a travel agent.
"I'm happy that we don't have a travel agent," Peter Long, Group Managing Director, told reporters.
Britain's Office of Fair Trading last month began a probe into the way vertically-integrated travel companies like Thomson and Airtours sell their holidays.
First Choice trades with a number of travel agents and enjoys being the UK's leading independent tour firm, Long said.

He said the company had sold 25 percent of its summer 1997 programme for UK customers by December 14, much earlier than its target date of the end of December, and that this will enable the company to plan business easier.
